title: Retrieve every SDDC Manager domain page in stable order
prompt:
Complete the root Go package `domaininventory` (module `vcf91-0035`, standard library only) as a focused VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager REST integration. The operator needs one complete domain inventory, even though `getDomains` is paginated, and repeated runs must emit byte-for-byte-equivalent collection order even when the appliance changes the order of elements within pages.

Before implementing, research the `getDomains` operation in the SDDC Manager OpenAPI specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository and cite the specification URLs consulted. Do not contact any other SDDC Manager route.

The public config, models, structured error types, and incomplete methods are in `client.go`. Preserve that public surface and implement these rules:

- `NewClient(Config)` treats `BaseURL` as an HTTP(S) origin and performs no traffic. Reject embedded credentials, query (including a dangling `?`), fragment, a non-root path, a blank or ASCII-whitespace-bearing access token, and a `PageSize` outside the positive signed int32 range required by the documented integer format. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Copy the selected HTTP client and disable redirect following without mutating the caller's client.
- `ListDomains(ctx)` rejects a nil client, nil context, or already-cancelled context locally. Preserve context cancellation through `errors.Is` and stop sending requests immediately after any failure.
- Invoke `getDomains` sequentially as exactly `GET /v1/domains?pageNumber=N&pageSize=S`, starting at one and requesting every page through `totalPages`. Send only the nondeprecated `pageNumber` and `pageSize` query parameters. Each GET has `Accept: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and has no Content-Type, body, transfer encoding, or extra route/query component.
- Accept exactly HTTP 200 with an `application/json` media type. Each success body must be one JSON document no larger than 1 MiB; reject malformed, trailing, or oversized success JSON with `*ProtocolError`.
- Treat the first page's `pageMetadata` as the pagination plan. Metadata values must be nonnegative signed int32 values, `pageNumber` must equal the requested page, and the returned `pageSize` must equal the number of elements in that response, as described by the specification. Require `totalPages` and `totalElements` to remain unchanged on later pages. A zero-page collection is valid only on the initial page-1 request with zero elements and zero totals. After the last page, require the collected count to equal `totalElements`.
- Preserve every decoded domain and field. Do not deduplicate or otherwise rewrite collection values. After all pages succeed, sort the complete slice by `name`, then by `id`, using Go's case-sensitive string ordering, and return a non-nil empty slice for an empty collection. Never return server order.
- Decode non-success JSON responses into `*APIError`, preserving operationId, HTTP status, errorCode, message, remediationMessage, and referenceToken. Use `*TransportError` for transport/read failures and keep its cause available to `errors.Is`/`errors.As`. Error strings must not expose the bearer token, response body, decoded server/remediation message, reference token, or underlying transport exception text.

Do not modify `go.mod`, `contract_test.go`, `.gitignore`, or `internal/contractmock/`; edit only `client.go`. Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`.
scenario: a complete paginated SDDC Manager domain inventory whose output order must remain stable across changing per-page server order
